summary: A genuinely mutual, English-law NDA that largely tracks the playbook, with deviations in the heightened carve-out evidence standard and narrowed independent development, no disclosure right for insurers, silence on compelled-disclosure costs, and an unmapped breach-notification duty.

findings.quote: disclosed by or on behalf of one Party
findings.why: Confidential Information is defined by reference to either Party as discloser, so the definition protects both sides.

findings.quote: each Party, acting as the Receiving Party, hereby covenants, undertakes and agrees with the other Party, acting as the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Obligations bind each Party as Receiving Party, so either party can be either role.

findings.quote: all information of whatever nature, form or media, whether oral, written, graphic, electronic, machine-readable or tangible, disclosed by or on behalf of one Party
findings.why: Definition is limited to information disclosed in connection with the Purpose and includes derived notes and analyses in (d), though it has no marked/reasonably-confidential test.

findings.quote: use the Confidential Information exclusively for the furtherance of the Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever
findings.why: Use is limited to the Purpose, which is a defined potential transaction, collaboration and integration partnership, slightly broader than the preferred wording.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: can conclusively demonstrate by contemporaneous written records, documentary evidence or other competent proof
findings.why: The evidence standard is 'conclusively' and 'contemporaneous', which is tougher than the playbook's 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence'.
findings.draft_redline: which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would prefer a standard of written records or reasonable evidence for the exclusions, rather than conclusive proof. This keeps the burden workable for both parties.

findings.quote: who had no access to, and did not make any use of or reference to, any Confidential Information disclosed by the Disclosing Party under this Agreement
findings.why: Independent development is narrowed to people with no access to any Confidential Information, which is stricter than a plain independent-development exception.
findings.draft_redline: was independently developed by or for the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We suggest the independent development exception turn on whether the Confidential Information was used, rather than on whether particular individuals had access. This is a common formulation and applies equally to both parties.

findings.quote: unless the combination as a whole and its economic value are in the public domain or in such prior possession
findings.why: The combination rule further narrows the carve-outs by treating combinations as confidential unless the whole combination and its economic value are public.
findings.draft_redline: unless the combination itself falls within one of the exceptions in Clause 3.1.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to simplify the combination wording so that a combination is excluded only where the combination itself falls within one of the listed exceptions.

findings.quote: the directors, officers, employees, legal advisers, financial auditors, technical consultants, accountants and professional agents of that Party or of any Affiliate of that Party
findings.why: Representatives cover employees, advisers, auditors and Affiliates on need-to-know with liability under 2.1.5, but insurers are not listed.
findings.draft_redline: the directors, officers, employees, legal advisers, financial auditors, insurers, technical consultants, accountants and professional agents of that Party or of any Affiliate of that Party
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please could we add insurers to the list of permitted Representatives, as each party may need to share information with its insurers on a need-to-know basis.

findings.quote: fully cooperate and consult with the Disclosing Party regarding the proposed timing, form, nature and extent of the mandatory disclosure
findings.why: Notice is qualified by 'subject to applicable legal restrictions' and 4.1.3 requires reasonable commercial efforts, but cooperation is not stated to be at the Disclosing Party's cost.
findings.draft_redline: cooperate with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party's cost, regarding the proposed timing, form, nature and extent of the mandatory disclosure; and
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to clarify that any cooperation or steps to resist or limit a compelled disclosure are at the cost of the party whose information is concerned.

findings.quote: within ten (10) Business Days following receipt of such request or upon such termination or expiration
findings.why: Return or destruction is within 10 Business Days with officer certification under 5.2.

findings.quote: electronic backup copies of Confidential Information generated automatically through routine data archiving, disaster recovery and electronic backup systems
findings.why: Automated backups and compliance copies may be retained and remain confidential under 5.4.

findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as granting, conferring, assigning or transferring
findings.why: No IP or licence passes; ownership stays with the Disclosing Party, and there is no feedback or improvements clause.

findings.quote: Neither the Disclosing Party nor any of its Representatives or Affiliates makes any representation or warranty regarding the accuracy, completeness, currency, reliability or utility of any Confidential Information disclosed hereunder.
findings.why: Mutual as-is and no-warranty disclaimers in reasonable wording; the reliance wording has no express fraud carve-out but nothing excludes liability for fraud.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: Neither this Agreement, nor the disclosure or receipt of any Confidential Information, shall constitute, create, imply or evidence an obligation by either Party to enter into any further commercial agreement
findings.why: States there is no obligation to proceed, as the playbook prefers.

findings.quote: the Parties shall negotiate in good faith and execute a separate, compliant data processing agreement or data sharing addendum prior to the transfer of any such personal data
findings.why: Limits personal data to business contact details and requires a separate DPA before any other sharing.

findings.quote: continue in full force and effect for a fixed period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Term is 3 years with 30 days' notice, within the accepted 1 to 3 year range.

findings.quote: shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years from the effective date of such expiration or termination
findings.why: Survival is 5 years, within the accepted 2 to 5 year range, with indefinite protection limited to Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: shall be entitled, without the necessity of posting any bond or other security, and without proving actual damages, to seek and obtain immediate injunctive relief
findings.why: Equitable relief is available to either Disclosing Party, so it is strongly worded but mutual, with no bond.
findings.fallback_cited: Strongly worded but mutual equitable relief.

findings.quote: shall be cumulative and shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, any other rights
findings.why: Remedies are expressly cumulative.

findings.quote: shall be governed by, construed, interpreted and enforced in accordance with the substantive laws of England and Wales
findings.why: Governing law is England and Wales.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction to settle, hear and determine any dispute
findings.why: Exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer, novate, charge, encumber, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations under this Agreement
findings.why: Mutual prohibition on assignment without prior written consent.

findings.quote: shall not, and shall ensure that its Representatives and Affiliates do not, reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble
findings.why: Prohibits reverse engineering of software and prototypes.

findings.quote: shall immediately notify the Disclosing Party in writing upon becoming aware of any actual, suspected or threatened unauthorised access
findings.why: An immediate duty to notify of actual, suspected or threatened breaches, with all reasonable cooperation, is not covered by any playbook rule.
